theater: 冰島西部外海與北大西洋漁場

battle.name: 第三次鱈魚戰爭
battle.theater: 冰島西部外海與北大西洋漁場
battle.brief: 第三次鱈魚戰爭是冰島與英國自1975年起，因北大西洋漁業資源及捕魚權引發的系列海上衝突，主要涉及漁船攔截、扣押與海警對峙。英國早期陸軍曾採用的步槍為恩菲爾德步槍（Enfield rifle，1858年）。

kit.name: 恩菲爾德步槍
kit.history: 恩菲爾德步槍是英國陸軍採用的制式步槍，配置於步兵分隊，主要供射擊、警戒與一般野戰任務使用。

countries: 第三次鱈魚戰爭不是有固定戰場與單一會戰時刻的傳統戰役，而是1975年10月至1976年6月英國與冰島在北大西洋漁業管轄上的低強度海上衝突。直接衝突的雙方只有兩國：冰島以海岸警衛隊執行二百海里漁業管轄，英國則由漁業主管機關、皇家海軍與外交部共同處理。挪威、美國及其他北約盟國提供斡旋、補給或外交支援，但不是對冰島作戰的一方。爭議海域位於冰島北方與西側外海，十二海里領海、五十海里漁業限制和冰島主張的二百海里區域是不同層級的法律與執法界線。英國是北約創始會員，冰島也是會員，卻長期不加入北約一體化軍事指揮，因此每次攔截都可能迅速變成盟國安全危機，而不能只視為漁船間的追逐。
countriesEn: The Third Cod War was not a conventional campaign with a fixed battlefield and a single moment of battle. It was a low-intensity maritime conflict between Iceland and the United Kingdom over fisheries jurisdiction from October 1975 to June 1976. The direct parties were Iceland, whose Coast Guard enforced a 200-nautical-mile fisheries jurisdiction, and the United Kingdom, whose response combined fisheries administration, the Royal Navy and the Foreign Office. Norway, the United States and other NATO members supplied mediation, replenishment or diplomatic support, but they were not belligerents. The disputed waters lay to the north and west of Iceland. The 12-nautical-mile territorial sea, the 50-nautical-mile fisheries limit and Iceland's claimed 200-nautical-mile zone were legally and operationally distinct lines. Britain was a NATO founder, and Iceland was also a member but had chosen to remain outside NATO's integrated military command. Consequently, every interception could quickly become an alliance crisis rather than merely a chase involving fishing vessels.
people: 政治責任主要落在兩國正式職位上。1975年時的冰島總理蓋爾·哈爾格里姆森主持政府，外長本尼迪克特·格倫達爾代表冰島處理漁業管轄與外交交涉；英國方面則由首相哈羅德·威爾斯主持政府，早期談判由外長戴維·歐文負責，1976年1月接任外交大臣的安東尼·克羅斯蘭延續談判。1976年2月19日宣布冰島與英國斷交的決定，代表冰島政府把管轄權爭議推到外交全面破裂的階段。北約秘書長約瑟夫·盧恩在盟國架構內穿梭協調，美國國務卿亨利·基辛格則促使華盛頓把事件視為北約共同風險。海上的實際行動由冰島海岸警衛隊與英國皇家海軍的專業指揮鏈執行，沒有一名高級政治人物直接指揮射擊。本文不虛構海上指揮官姓名，也不把外交官員的作用寫成單一個人親自解決危機。
peopleEn: Political responsibility rested with the formal officeholders of the two governments. Iceland's Prime Minister Geir Hallgrímsson led the government in 1975, while Foreign Minister Benedikt Gröndal represented Iceland in the fisheries-jurisdiction dispute and in diplomatic dealings. In Britain, Prime Minister Harold Wilson headed the government. Foreign Secretary David Owen led the early negotiations, and Anthony Crosland, who became Foreign Secretary in January 1976, continued them. On 19 February 1976, the decision to sever diplomatic relations with the United Kingdom carried Iceland's jurisdictional dispute into a complete diplomatic rupture. NATO Secretary-General Joseph Luns coordinated among the allies, while United States Secretary of State Henry Kissinger pressed Washington to treat the confrontation as a NATO-wide risk. Operational actions at sea remained under the professional command structures of the Icelandic Coast Guard and the Royal Navy. No senior political leader personally directed gunfire. This account does not invent the names of naval commanders or imply that one diplomat single-handedly resolved the crisis.
kits: 冰島海岸警衛隊的核心裝備包括1959年服役的Þór號、1966年服役的Ægir號、1970年服役的Esja號，以及1973年服役的Freyja號巡邏艦。它們以Bofors 40毫米L/60或57毫米L/60艦炮為主要武備，部分艦另配Oerlikon 20毫米砲與機槍，並帶有搜索雷達、無線電及供小型直升機使用的甲板設施；近岸巡邏艇和截斷漁網具的特裝艇則負責貼近漁船。英方海上支援由在役的Leander級、Type 21、Type 22護衛艦和Type 42驅逐艦輪替提供，這些艦載有4.5吋Mk 6主炮、Oerlikon 20毫米砲、Seacat或Sea Dart飛彈，以及Westland Wasp或Westland Lynx直升機；Sea Dart在1973年已列裝，Wasp與Lynx亦分別在1963年和1969年進入英軍服役。可確認的警告射擊主要來自冰島海警艦炮或機槍，沒有可靠紀錄顯示英方發射Sea Dart、4.5吋主炮或以直升機攻擊海警船。英軍由本土北大西洋基地取得燃油、補給與飛行支援；冰島巡邏艦則以雷克雅未克為主要基地往返爭議海域，依短程任務補充燃料和彈藥。
kitsEn: The Icelandic Coast Guard's principal capability consisted of the patrol vessels Þór, commissioned in 1959; Ægir, commissioned in 1966; Esja, commissioned in 1970; and Freyja, commissioned in 1973. Their principal weapons were Bofors 40 mm L/60 or 57 mm L/60 naval guns, with some ships also carrying Oerlikon 20 mm weapons and machine guns, supported by search radar, radio equipment and helicopter-capable decks. Small coastal patrol craft and specially equipped cutters allowed the service to approach fishing vessels closely and sever their fishing gear. British maritime support was provided in rotation by operational Leander-class, Type 21 and Type 22 frigates and Type 42 destroyers. Their equipment included the 4.5-inch Mk 6 gun, Oerlikon 20 mm weapons, Seacat or Sea Dart missiles, and Westland Wasp or Westland Lynx helicopters. Sea Dart had entered service in 1973, while Wasp and Lynx had entered Royal Navy service in 1963 and 1969 respectively. The warning fire that can be confirmed came from Icelandic Coast Guard guns or machine guns. There is no reliable evidence that British forces fired Sea Dart or the 4.5-inch guns, or used their helicopters to attack Coast Guard vessels. British ships obtained fuel, stores and aviation support from bases in Britain, while Icelandic patrols worked from Reykjavík, returning to port for fuel and ammunition on relatively short missions.
tactics: Immediate operational effects included warning fire across the bows of British fishing vessels, Coast Guard approaches, boarding parties, temporary detention and the seizure or cutting of fishing gear. Fishing work in the contested sectors was repeatedly interrupted, and British naval escorts had to remain close enough to observe the Coast Guard while avoiding circumstances that could be presented as an armed attack by the United Kingdom. Diplomatically, Iceland's announcement on 19 February 1976 ended the high-level talks at a stage when the substantive fisheries formula remained disputed. Britain's response was to suspend the talks and adjust its naval posture, while Iceland retained enforcement of the wider limit. The dispute also exposed an alliance problem: Iceland was a NATO member but outside the integrated military structure, Britain depended on maritime and diplomatic support from fellow members, and the United States had a major security role in Iceland. NATO consultation and the involvement of the United States therefore concentrated pressure on both governments to restore negotiations before an accidental naval clash could escalate the matter. These effects remained operational and governmental; they did not become a sustained fleet battle, and available records do not confirm a combat death.
tacticsEn: The immediate operational effects included warning fire across the bows of British fishing vessels, Coast Guard approaches, boarding parties, temporary detention and the seizure or cutting of fishing gear. Fishing operations in the contested sectors were repeatedly interrupted. British naval escorts remained close enough to observe the Coast Guard while avoiding circumstances that could be presented as an armed attack by the United Kingdom. Diplomatically, Iceland's announcement on 19 February 1976 ended high-level talks at a point when the substantive fisheries formula was still disputed. Britain suspended negotiations and adjusted its naval posture, while Iceland maintained enforcement of the wider limit. The dispute also exposed an alliance problem. Iceland was a NATO member but remained outside the integrated military structure; Britain depended on maritime and diplomatic support from fellow members; and the United States had a major security role in Iceland. NATO consultation and United States involvement consequently concentrated pressure on both governments to resume negotiations before an accidental clash could escalate further. The effects remained operational and governmental. There was no sustained fleet battle, and available records do not confirm a combat death.
data: 按可核對的年代次序，1952年英冰先就英國漁船進入冰島附近海域達成權利交換，1961年的漁業安排則確認冰島五十海里限制及英方配額安排，解決的是第一場鱈魚戰爭留下的問題。1974年，冰島議會通過二百海里漁業管轄法律，該法於1975年10月15日生效。10月下旬起，冰島海警開始攔查進入主張海域的英籍漁船；11月初出現密集登檢、漁具截留及警告射擊，英國隨後加派皇家海軍掩護漁船，雙方在1975年冬季與1976年初繼續談判，但未就漁區、總量配額和執法方式達成協議。1976年2月19日，冰島宣布與英國斷交，談判中斷；2月下旬至5月由北約盟國與美國展開降溫外交。1976年6月1日，英冰簽署新的漁業協議，戰爭的主要對抗階段因而結束。現有官方與標準史料沒有提供可核實的第三次衝突死亡總數，也沒有可靠依據把第二次戰爭的射擊紀錄移用於本戰，因此本文只確認有警告射擊、登檢、漁具損壞、扣留與外交危機，不列任何精確傷亡數字。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology begins with the 1952 Anglo-Icelandic exchange of notes concerning British fishing access near Iceland. The 1961 fisheries arrangement recognized Iceland's 50-nautical-mile limit and addressed British quota access, settling the principal issue left by the First Cod War. In 1974, Iceland's parliament adopted legislation establishing a 200-nautical-mile fisheries jurisdiction, which took effect on 15 October 1975. Late that month, the Coast Guard began intercepting British fishing vessels inside the claimed zone. Early November brought concentrated boardings, removal of fishing gear and warning fire, after which the United Kingdom increased Royal Navy protection and the two sides continued negotiations through the winter and early 1976 without agreement on fishing areas, total quotas or enforcement. On 19 February 1976, Iceland announced the severing of diplomatic relations with the United Kingdom and negotiations broke down. From late February through May, NATO members and the United States worked to lower the temperature. A new fisheries agreement followed on 1 June 1976, ending the main confrontational phase. Official and standard reference accounts do not provide a verifiable total of deaths for this conflict, and there is no sound basis for transferring firing figures from the earlier Cod War into this one. This account therefore confirms warning fire, boardings, damaged fishing gear, detentions and a diplomatic crisis without inventing casualty numbers.
cause: 在二百海里法律生效後，真正引發持續衝突的是執法與談判之間的落差。冰島海岸警衛隊把二百海里視為完整的漁業管轄範圍，要求英籍漁船取得冰島許可並接受登檢；英國則認為既有交換文件與漁業安排仍有效，漁船進入指定海域不應由英方一概視為非法。英方海軍提供掩護後，海警與漁船之間每次近距離接觸都增加了碰撞、警告射擊或誤判的風險。漁業主管機關同時計算漁獲、漁區與年度總量，避免單純的執法事件在談判中變成更大的政治挑戰。冰島面對的是長期依賴漁業收益的經濟結構，英國面對的則是遠洋漁業船隊、港口就業及既有捕撈配額；雙方都知道全面讓步會改變各自政策。因此衝突一直維持在登檢、警告射擊、護航與外交施壓的層次，直到北約盟國介入，要求把執法問題重新放回可談的配額與區域安排。
causeEn: Once the 200-nautical-mile legal claim took effect, the continuing conflict arose from the gap between enforcement and negotiation. The Icelandic Coast Guard treated the full 200-nautical-mile area as a fisheries jurisdiction, required British vessels to obtain Icelandic permission and accepted boarding and inspection as conditions of access. Britain maintained that the earlier exchanges and fisheries arrangements remained relevant and did not accept wholesale exclusion. Once Royal Navy escorts were present, every close encounter between a patrol ship and a fishing vessel increased the risk of collision, warning fire or miscalculation. Fisheries administrators also assessed catches, areas and annual totals so that enforcement incidents did not automatically become larger political claims. Iceland's economy depended heavily on fisheries, while Britain had a distant-water fleet, port employment and established quotas at stake. Each government understood that a complete concession would amount to a fundamental policy change. The confrontation was therefore confined to boarding, warning fire, escort operations and diplomatic pressure until NATO allies intervened and required both sides to return the dispute to a negotiable system of quotas and designated fishing areas.
impact: 對海上行動而言，衝突把原本可以由漁業談判處理的問題變成了每天都可能發生登檢與警告射擊的局面。冰島漁船執法不再只限於較近岸的傳統漁區，而是在整個二百海里主張範圍內持續存在；英國皇家海軍因而需要反覆調整護航、偵察與通報安排，使英籍漁船可以在指定海域作業，同時避免護航艦與海警船發生直接衝突。外交層面的破壞更為明顯：冰島在1976年2月19日與英國斷交，原先的談判渠道全部停止，直到北約與美國重新建立接觸才得以恢復。這場危機也迫使盟國正視北約會員之間的權限爭議，以及一國拒絕納入北約軍事指揮結構後所產生的安全矛盾。可核對的史料沒有確認交火造成死亡，因此不應把未經核實的人員數字當作傷亡總結；實際影響主要落在漁船扣留、漁網具損壞、航行作業中斷、外交代表撤回及盟國外交資源的投入。
impactEn: At sea, the conflict turned a dispute that could have been handled through fisheries negotiations into one in which boarding and warning fire could occur repeatedly. Icelandic enforcement no longer remained confined to the older coastal grounds and continued throughout the claimed 200-nautical-mile area. The Royal Navy consequently had to revise escort, observation and reporting arrangements so that British vessels could work in designated areas without allowing escorts and Coast Guard ships to collide. The diplomatic damage was more direct. Iceland severed relations with the United Kingdom on 19 February 1976, and the existing negotiating channels stopped until NATO and the United States established new contact. The crisis also forced allies to confront a jurisdictional dispute between NATO members and the security complications created by Iceland's exclusion from NATO's integrated military structure. Verifiable records do not confirm deaths caused by the gunfire, so unverified personnel figures should not be presented as a casualty total. The measurable effects were instead the detention of fishing vessels, damaged net gear, interrupted fishing operations, the withdrawal of diplomatic representatives and the diversion of allied diplomatic resources.
result: 1976年6月1日，英國與冰島達成新的漁業協議。英國接受冰島對二百海里漁業區的管轄，不再要求其漁船不受該區域規則約束；冰島則允許英籍漁船在指定海域內按年度總量配額作業，並接受由海岸警衛隊執行檢查與執法。這不是恢復英方不受限制的捕撈權，也不是完全禁止英國漁船進入，而是以海域、配額和監管方式限制通行。各階段部署的英國護衛艦與驅逐艦離開危機部署，返回北大西洋常態任務；冰島海警則繼續在二百海里線內巡邏，協議因此終結了以斷交、密集警告射擊和近距離追截為主的對抗階段。協議本身仍有期限，並留下漁區界定、配額分配、檢查程序及後續續約等問題，所以它結束的是這場危機，不是所有漁業爭端。現有可核對資料沒有足以支持精確傷亡統計的紀錄，本文不作數字推定。
resultEn: On 1 June 1976, the United Kingdom and Iceland reached a new fisheries agreement. Britain accepted Iceland's jurisdiction over the 200-nautical-mile fisheries zone and no longer demanded that its vessels remain wholly outside that area. Iceland in turn allowed British fishing vessels to operate within designated waters under an annual total quota and accepted inspection and enforcement by its Coast Guard. This was not a restoration of unrestricted British fishing rights, nor a complete prohibition on British vessels. Access was instead regulated through defined areas, a total quota and Icelandic supervision. British frigates and destroyers withdrawn from the crisis posture and returned to routine North Atlantic duties, while Icelandic patrols continued within the claimed 200-nautical-mile line. The agreement therefore ended the phase dominated by diplomatic rupture, repeated warning fire and close pursuit. It did not eliminate every fisheries dispute: the duration of the arrangement, boundaries, quota distribution, inspection procedures and later renewal remained subjects of negotiation. What ended was the acute confrontation, not all disagreement over access. The verifiable records do not support a precise casualty total, so this account makes no numerical estimate.
